```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
# All preparation and plotting logic is in this document.
# scripts/prepare_data.R executes only the first two chunks as an R entry point.
# Default: render from the committed small data subset.
# Rebuild: -P refresh_data:true -P raw_dir:"folder/containing/both/gzip/files"
# Download and rebuild: -P download_raw:true -P refresh_data:true
dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("output/figures", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
raw_dir <- params$raw_dir
if (isTRUE(params$download_raw)) {
  dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  base_url <- "https://data.insideairbnb.com/taiwan/northern-taiwan/taipei/2026-09-28/data/"
  for (name in c("listings.csv.gz", "calendar.csv.gz")) {
    target <- file.path(raw_dir, name)
    if (!file.exists(target)) download.file(paste0(base_url, name), target, mode = "wb")
  }
}
rebuild <- isTRUE(params$refresh_data) ||
  !all(file.exists(file.path("data/processed", c("listings_subset.csv", "audit.csv", "calendar_monthly.csv"))))
```

```{r}
#| label: prepare-real-data
#| include: false
if (rebuild) {
  dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  read_gz <- function(path) {
    # Preserve UTF-8 bytes instead of transcoding through the Windows locale.
    con <- gzfile(path, "rt")
    on.exit(close(con))
    read.csv(con, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE,
             na.strings = c("", "NA"), encoding = "UTF-8")
  }
  listings_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "listings.csv.gz")
  calendar_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "calendar.csv.gz")
  stopifnot(file.exists(listings_path), file.exists(calendar_path))
  l <- read_gz(listings_path)
  c <- read_gz(calendar_path)
  needed <- c("id", "last_scraped", "minimum_nights", "price", "room_type",
              "neighbourhood_cleansed", "accommodates", "price_quote_raw",
              "price_quote_checkin_date", "price_quote_checkout_date")
  stopifnot(all(needed %in% names(l)), all(c("listing_id", "date", "available", "minimum_nights", "maximum_nights") %in% names(c)))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(l$id), !anyDuplicated(l$id))
  stopifnot(!anyNA(c$listing_id), !anyNA(c$date),
            !anyDuplicated(c[c("listing_id", "date")]), all(c$listing_id %in% l$id),
            all(c$available %in% c("t", "f")))
  currency <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(l))
  has_currency <- !is.na(l$price_quote_raw) & grepl('"currency"\\s*:', l$price_quote_raw)
  currency[has_currency] <- sub('.*"currency"\\s*:\\s*"([^"]+)".*', '\\1', l$price_quote_raw[has_currency])
  cleaned <- l %>%
    mutate(
      minimum_nights = suppressWarnings(as.integer(minimum_nights)),
      valid_minimum = !is.na(minimum_nights) & minimum_nights >= 1,
      price_number = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub("[$,]", "", price))),
      quote_currency = currency,
      valid_price = is.finite(price_number) & price_number > 0 &
        !is.na(quote_currency) & quote_currency == "TWD",
      stay_group = case_when(
        !valid_minimum ~ NA_character_,
        minimum_nights <= 2 ~ "1-2 nights",
        minimum_nights <= 6 ~ "3-6 nights",
        TRUE ~ "7+ nights"
      ),
      quoted_nightly_price_twd = if_else(valid_price, price_number, NA_real_),
      accommodates = suppressWarnings(as.integer(accommodates)),
      quote_stay_nights = as.integer(as.Date(price_quote_checkout_date) - as.Date(price_quote_checkin_date))
    )
  d <- cleaned %>%
    select(listing_id = id, last_scraped, minimum_nights, stay_group, room_type,
      neighbourhood_cleansed, accommodates, quoted_nightly_price_twd, quote_currency,
      quote_checkin = price_quote_checkin_date, quote_checkout = price_quote_checkout_date,
      quote_stay_nights)
  write.csv(d, "data/processed/listings_subset.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
  monthly <- c %>%
    mutate(month = substr(date, 1, 7)) %>%
    group_by(month) %>%
    summarise(calendar_rows = n(), listings = n_distinct(listing_id),
      dates = n_distinct(date), available_rows = sum(available == "t"), .groups = "drop")
  write.csv(monthly, "data/processed/calendar_monthly.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  audit <- data.frame(metric = c("listings", "calendar_rows", "calendar_listings", "calendar_start", "calendar_end",
      "duplicate_listing_ids", "duplicate_listing_dates", "invalid_minimum_nights",
      "valid_positive_twd_prices", "missing_or_invalid_or_non_twd_prices", "calendar_has_price",
      "raw_listings_md5", "raw_calendar_md5"),
    value = c(nrow(l), nrow(c), length(unique(c$listing_id)), min(c$date), max(c$date), 0, 0,
      sum(!cleaned$valid_minimum), sum(cleaned$valid_price), sum(!cleaned$valid_price), "price" %in% names(c),
      unname(tools::md5sum(listings_path)), unname(tools::md5sum(calendar_path))))
  write.csv(audit, "data/processed/audit.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(c("Calendar columns:", paste(names(c), collapse = ", "),
               "Calendar contains no date-level prices in this supplied release."), "data/processed/schema_note.txt")
  rm(l, c)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: descriptive-summaries
#| include: false
d <- read.csv("data/processed/listings_subset.csv", colClasses = c(listing_id = "character"),
              na.strings = "", encoding = "UTF-8") %>%
  mutate(
    stay_group = factor(stay_group, levels = c("1-2 nights", "3-6 nights", "7+ nights")),
    valid_rule = !is.na(stay_group),
    valid_price = is.finite(quoted_nightly_price_twd) & quoted_nightly_price_twd > 0
  )
# Separate weekly-length and monthly-length minimum-stay rules.
detailed_data <- d %>%
  mutate(
    detailed_stay_group = case_when(
      is.na(minimum_nights) | minimum_nights < 1 ~ NA_character_,
      minimum_nights <= 2 ~ "1-2 nights",
      minimum_nights <= 6 ~ "3-6 nights",
      minimum_nights <= 29 ~ "7-29 nights",
      TRUE ~ "30+ nights"
    ),
    detailed_stay_group = factor(
      detailed_stay_group,
      levels = c("1-2 nights", "3-6 nights",
                 "7-29 nights", "30+ nights")
    )
  )

# Measure usable and missing/unusable prices within each group.
stay_group_quality <- detailed_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(detailed_stay_group)) %>%
  group_by(detailed_stay_group) %>%
  summarise(
    total_listings = n(),
    usable_prices = sum(valid_price),
    missing_prices = sum(!valid_price),
    missing_percent = 100 * mean(!valid_price),
    median_twd = median(quoted_nightly_price_twd[valid_price]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write.csv(
  stay_group_quality,
  "data/processed/stay_group_quality.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

audit <- read.csv("data/processed/audit.csv", colClasses = "character")
audit_value <- function(key) audit$value[match(key, audit$metric)]
price_data <- d %>% filter(valid_price)
comparison_data <- price_data %>% filter(valid_rule)
group_counts <- d %>% filter(valid_rule) %>% count(stay_group, name = "listings") %>%
  mutate(share_percent = 100 * listings / sum(listings))
group_prices <- comparison_data %>% group_by(stay_group) %>%
  summarise(valid_price_n = n(), median_twd = median(quoted_nightly_price_twd),
    q1_twd = quantile(quoted_nightly_price_twd, .25),
    q3_twd = quantile(quoted_nightly_price_twd, .75), .groups = "drop")
stats <- group_counts %>% left_join(group_prices, by = "stay_group")
distribution <- price_data %>% summarise(
  listings = n(), median_twd = median(quoted_nightly_price_twd),
  q1_twd = quantile(quoted_nightly_price_twd, .25),
  q3_twd = quantile(quoted_nightly_price_twd, .75),
  p90_twd = quantile(quoted_nightly_price_twd, .90),
  max_twd = max(quoted_nightly_price_twd),
  above_10000_percent = 100 * mean(quoted_nightly_price_twd > 10000)
)
stopifnot(nrow(d) == as.integer(audit_value("listings")), all(stats$valid_price_n > 0))
write.csv(stats, "data/processed/figure_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(distribution, "data/processed/price_distribution_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)
money <- function(x) format(round(x, 2), nsmall = 2, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
plot_theme <- theme_gray(base_size = 11) + theme(
  legend.position = "none", plot.title = element_text(size = 12),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.title = element_text(size = 10),
  plot.margin = margin(8, 10, 8, 8)
)
price_breaks <- c(300, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000, 100000)
figure1 <- ggplot(price_data, aes(x = quoted_nightly_price_twd)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = .1, boundary = 0, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white", linewidth = .2) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = price_breaks, labels = fmt) +
  labs(x = "Quoted nightly price (TWD, logarithmic scale)", y = "Number of listings") +
  plot_theme
# Keep usable prices with a known minimum-stay group.
comparison_detail <- detailed_data %>%
  filter(valid_price, !is.na(detailed_stay_group))

group_labels <- paste0(
  as.character(stay_group_quality$detailed_stay_group),
  "\n(n = ", fmt(stay_group_quality$usable_prices), ")"
)

figure2 <- ggplot(
  comparison_detail,
  aes(x = detailed_stay_group, y = quoted_nightly_price_twd)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "steelblue", outlier.alpha = .35,
    outlier.size = .8, linewidth = .4
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = group_labels) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = price_breaks, labels = fmt) +
  labs(
    x = "Listing-level minimum-stay requirement",
    y = "Quoted nightly price (TWD, log scale)"
  ) +
  plot_theme
# Check that the histogram includes every eligible real price.
stopifnot(sum(ggplot_build(figure1)$data[[1]]$count) == nrow(price_data))
ggsave("output/figures/figure_1.png", figure1, width = 7, height = 3.1, dpi = 250)
ggsave("output/figures/figure_2.png", figure2, width = 7, height = 3.2, dpi = 250)
```

## Research question

Do Taipei Airbnb listings with longer minimum-night requirements exhibit smaller differences in advertised nightly prices between candidate high- and low-demand periods? More stable pricing could help travelers choose when and how long to stay, and help hosts evaluate booking rules. We hypothesize that listings targeting longer stays may have smaller seasonal premiums; this is an observational question about association.

## Data overview

We use Inside Airbnb's **September 28, 2026 Taipei release**, comprising `r fmt(nrow(d))` listings scraped September 28-29. Each observation is a listing. We group minimum-stay requirements into 1-2, 3-6, 7-29, and 30+ nights, separating the original 7+ category into two groups. One listing lacks a minimum-stay rule. Quoted prices refer to different check-in dates and stay lengths.

## Figure 1: Distribution of quoted nightly prices

```{r}
#| label: fig-price-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of positive nightly quotes (n = 5,868). Bins have width 0.1 on the log10 price scale (about 26% price increments). Source: Inside Airbnb; team calculations."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 2.8
figure1
```

The median quote is **TWD `r money(distribution$median_twd)`**, with the middle half between TWD `r money(distribution$q1_twd)` and `r money(distribution$q3_twd)`. Prices have a long upper tail: `r sprintf("%.1f", distribution$above_10000_percent)`% exceed TWD 10,000, and the maximum is TWD `r money(distribution$max_twd)`. The log scale keeps this tail visible; all positive TWD quotes are retained. This spread motivates comparing typical prices within listings rather than relying on cross-sectional averages, which can be sensitive to unusually expensive properties.

\newpage

## Figure 2: Quoted prices by minimum-stay group

```{r}
#| label: fig-price-groups
#| fig-cap: "Nightly quote distributions by minimum-stay rule (n = 5,867). Boxes and 1.5-IQR whiskers are calculated on log10 prices; dots show values beyond the whiskers. Source: Inside Airbnb; team calculations."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.2
figure2
```

Median nightly quotes are **TWD `r money(stay_group_quality$median_twd[1])`** for 1-2-night requirements, **TWD `r money(stay_group_quality$median_twd[2])`** for 3-6 nights, **TWD `r money(stay_group_quality$median_twd[3])`** for 7-29 nights, and **TWD `r money(stay_group_quality$median_twd[4])`** for 30+ nights. The first two groups have similar medians. Separating the original 7+ category reveals a lower median for 30+ nights than for 7-29 nights, although their distributions overlap.

The figure includes `r fmt(nrow(comparison_detail))` listings with positive usable prices and known minimum-stay rules; no eligible positive prices are trimmed. Missing or unusable prices account for **`r sprintf("%.1f", stay_group_quality$missing_percent[1])`%, `r sprintf("%.1f", stay_group_quality$missing_percent[2])`%, `r sprintf("%.1f", stay_group_quality$missing_percent[3])`%, and `r sprintf("%.1f", stay_group_quality$missing_percent[4])`%** of all listings in the four respective groups. Longer-stay groups therefore have less complete price coverage. Their observed price distributions may not represent listings with missing quotes; the direction of any resulting bias is unknown.

These findings motivate retaining separate 7-29 and 30+ groups and examining missing-price coverage in the planned analysis. Lower price levels do not establish smaller seasonal premiums. Differences in quote dates, stay lengths, discounts, room types, and locations may explain the observed patterns. Testing seasonal stability still requires suitable date-level prices.

## Planned analysis and feasibility

Before the main analysis, we must obtain a source of date-level advertised prices or revise the research question. The supplied `r fmt(as.integer(audit_value("calendar_rows")))` calendar rows record availability and stay restrictions, not prices. Availability cannot substitute for price or bookings: an unavailable night may be host-blocked.

If suitable prices become available, we plan to retain listings with usable prices in both periods, calculate each listing's monthly median price, and compare the percentage difference $100(P_{i,D}-P_{i,A})/P_{i,A}$ across minimum-stay groups, where $D$ and $A$ denote December and August. We would examine room type, neighbourhood, guest capacity, missingness, and separate weekly/monthly requirements. Demand evidence is needed before labeling either month high or low season; unequal booking lead times also limit interpretation. These figures provide descriptive motivation, not a seasonal test or a causal estimate.
